title: Reconstructing fluid velocity fields from sparse sensors using a variational quantum algorithm
authors: Nhat-Quang Nguyen, Mohammad Mehedi Hasan Akash, Kourosh Shoele, Yanzhu Chen, Huixuan Wu
abstract: Reconstructing fields governed by nonlinear partial differential equations (PDEs) from sparse measurements is a challenging task because the governing equations are strongly nonlinear and observations are available at only a few locations. Fluid velocity fields are a representative case. In this paper, we propose a variational quantum algorithm that reconstructs the solution over the entire spacetime domain at once. Rather than marching in time, the method encodes the full discrete spacetime solution in a single variational quantum state, so that all time points are optimized jointly. The cost function combines a sparse-measurement mismatch term with a physics-informed PDE violation term, letting data and the governing equation constrain the solution simultaneously. We demonstrate the method on the one-dimensional Burgers and Kuramoto--Sivashinsky equations using numerical simulations. The results suggest that variational quantum algorithms with a spacetime encoding scheme offer a compact framework for reconstructing nonlinear PDE dynamics.
summary: This paper introduces a variational quantum algorithm to reconstruct fluid velocity fields from sparse sensor data by encoding the entire spacetime solution into a single quantum state. It minimizes a cost function that simultaneously enforces the governing nonlinear PDE and matches sparse measurements. The method shows promise for quantum-enhanced solutions to complex, time-dependent physical inverse problems.
main_problem: The core challenge is reconstructing continuous physical fields governed by nonlinear Partial Differential Equations (PDEs) when measurements are available only at sparse locations.
main_result: The authors demonstrate that a variational quantum algorithm employing a spacetime-encoding scheme can successfully reconstruct globally consistent spacetime fields from sparse observations with low Root-Mean-Square (RMS) error.
method: They propose a VQA framework where the entire discrete spacetime solution is encoded into a single quantum state, optimizing all time points jointly by minimizing a cost function combining PDE violation and measurement mismatch.
model_or_system: The method is applied to fluid velocity fields, specifically modeling the one-dimensional Burgers and Kuramoto-Sivashinsky (KS) equations under periodic boundary conditions.
key_observables: Root-Mean-Square (RMS) error quantifying reconstruction accuracy; the reconstructed velocity field u(t, x).
important_parameters: Viscosity parameter ($\nu$); time and space discretization steps ($\Delta t, \Delta x$); the weighting hyperparameter ($w$) balancing PDE and measurement constraints.
main_assumptions: The solution must admit a sparse representation within the Hilbert space accessible by the chosen quantum ansatz; the real-space approach uses first-order finite-difference approximations for derivatives.
figures_summary: Figures show reconstructed velocity fields for the Burgers and KS equations under varying resolutions, and a comparison of final-time wave profiles for both equations.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from the general inverse problem challenge to proposing the VQA framework. It details two implementation strategies (real-space vs. Galerkin-reduced-basis) for encoding the physics constraint into the quantum cost function, culminating in numerical simulations and results.
why_interesting: This work directly applies quantum computation to solve a complex, continuous, non-equilibrium physics problem (PDEs), offering a quantum-enhanced approach to inverse problems in fluid dynamics.
